The amount of progress gained will depend on the player's Mining level, the tier of pickaxe that they use and their current ''stamina'' level. Additionally, 10% of the player's [[Strength]] level is added to the player's progress gains. Rocks have two assigned stats, ''durability'' and ''hardness''. ... Once the player has built up enough progress points to equal the rock's durability, they will gain ore and their progress will reset. ====Hardness==== '''Hardness''' reduces the amount of progress gained from mining the rock and is checked against [[Mining#Penetration|penetration]]. ... '''Penetration''' is a stat that is checked against the [[Mining#Hardness|hardness]] of the rock attempting to be mined. If the pickaxes' penetration stat is less than the hardness level of the rock the damage done toward an ore is reduced, and a chat message {{RSFont|Your pickaxe is a lower level than this mining node, so you are getting reduced rates.|color=#EB2F2F}} appears. As experience is granted relative to the amount of damage dealt, this also reduces the amount of experience gained per swing. ====Damage (stat)==== '''Damage''' is a stat that determines the base damage a pickaxe can do. It is generally a range. As the level of a pickaxe increases, so does the damage stat. :'''For example:''' a [[bronze pickaxe]] has a minimum damage stat of 3 and a maximum damage stat of 7. In contrast, a [[Dragon pickaxe]] has a minimum damage stat of 33 and a maximum damage stat of 93. As a general rule the better the pickaxe, the more effective it is as a mining tool. ... Each swing deals damage based on the players Mining level, Strength level, and the pickaxe used. Swings occur every 4 ticks (2.4 seconds). If a player's Strength level vastly out-levels their Mining level, it has a huge impact on their damage per swing and in turn their ore and experience per hour. Damage progress is stored even if a player stops mining or switches rocks, provided they resume mining the same type of rock. ====Basic equation==== The basic calculation for damage is: \text{Damage Per Swing} = \text{Mining level} + \left\lfloor \frac{\text{Strength level}}{10} \right\rfloor + \text{Damage Roll + Crit Bonus} + min (\text{Net Hardness}, 0) =====Equation notes===== * \text{Net} \text{ Hardness} is calculated by the formula \text{Net Hardness} = \text{Penetration} - \text{Hardness}. The minimum of 0 and \text{Net} \text{ Hardness} is added to the damage per swing. If this is a negative number, the damage per swing is reduced. Otherwise it is unaffected. ::'''For example:''' :::{| class="wikitable" ! Levels ! Pickaxe ! Rock ! Damage per swing |- align="center" | rowspan="2" | {{Skill clickpic|Mining|30}}

30 hardness | 6 - 10 |- align="center" | [[Mithril pickaxe]]: 15-45 damage
30 penetration | 48 - 78 |} * \text{Crit }\text{Bonus} is only added to the equation if the swing deals a critical hit. By default the player has a 10% chance on each swing to deal a critical strike, this is increased as the players mining level increases. ... The equation will take into account a level '''+ 4 bonus''' to the damage per swing as opposed to a '''+ 3 bonus.''' * Any excess damage carries over to your progress to another ore. However, more than 100% of the durability of a rock cannot be dealt in a single swing. Anything above 100% will be capped at 100%. ::'''For example:''' ... | 40-40This would guarantee an ore every swing. |} ===Stamina=== [[File:Full stamina.gif|thumb|A player with full stamina|250px]] At Mining level 15, players unlock the ''stamina'' multiplier mechanic of the damage formula. Every swing drains 10 stamina, but stamina is refilled completely upon clicking a rock. ... (i.e., level 1-10 Agility would provide 1 extra swing, level 31-40 Agility would provide 4 extra swings). Therefore, the minimum stamina is 31 (30 from Mining and 1 from Agility), giving a minimum of 4 swings before running out. [[Temporary skill boost]]s which cause a visible increase in the player's Agility level do affect the calculation of stamina. At 88+ Mining and 91+ Agility, a player's stamina will last for 21 swings (50.4 seconds). As stamina improves, so does the damage per hour for semi-active players. The mechanic supports both active and semi-active gameplay. Active mining requires the player to maintain full stamina by clicking the rock once every 4 ticks (2.4 s). ... rowspan="2" | Rock ! colspan="3" | Damage per swing |- ! Full stamina ! Since damage progress doesn't reset for changing to other rocks of the same type, participating in rockertunities can increase experience and ore per hour. They also have the potential to deal a critical hit, further increasing damage and experience. Using rockertunities also eliminates the random roll from the damage calculation, always resulting in average damage rounded down to the nearest integer being dealt. ... Once spawned, a rockertunity will only disappear when the player starts mining that rock, leaves the area or starts mining a different type of rock. ====Rockertunity multiplier==== While the base multiplier for rockertunities is \times 4, higher Mining levels can raise the multiplier to \times 6 (dependent on rock). The values on the table below correspond to the Mining level required for the increased multipliers. This levelling benefit only applies to core rocks, so, when mining [[concentrated coal]], the rockertunity multiplier will always be four. Rocks that do not give core ore at all do not have rockertunities. The [[magic golem outfit]] and the [[Brooch of the Gods]] both increase this limit by \times1 each, so the maximum multiplier is \times7 or \times8, depending on the ore being mined. {| class="wikitable align-left-1 align-center-2 align-center-3 align-center-4 sortable" ! rowspan="2" | Rock ! colspan="3" | Level requirement for rockertunity multiplier |- ! x4 ! x5 ! x6 |- | [[Copper rock]] | rowspan="2" | 1 | rowspan="2" | 6 | {{NA}} |- | [[Tin rock]] | {{NA}} |- | [[Iron rock]] | 10 | 14 | {{NA}} |- | [[Coal rock]] | 20 | 21 | {{NA}} |- | [[Mithril rock]] | 30 | 38 | {{NA}} |- | [[Adamantite rock]] | rowspan="2" | 40 ... | [[Katagon rock]] |- | [[Gorgonite rock]] |- | [[Promethium rock]] |} ====Example==== {| class="wikitable" ! If a critical swing is rolled on a rockertunity swing, the rockertunity multiplier also applies to the additional damage from the critical effect. A popup occurs whenever a critical swing is hit: [[File:Critical swing hitsplat.png]] ====Critical swing chance==== By default the player has a 10% chance on each swing to deal a critical swing. This base critical chance increases to 15% at level 59 Mining, and to 20% at level 85. Additionally, reaching specific level thresholds offers higher critical swing chances, specific to each rock. This levelling benefit only applies to core rocks, so, when mining non-core rocks such as concentrated coal or gold, the base critical hit chance will be used. This benefit stacks with the aforementioned base critical chance increases. For example, players mining runite rock at level 60 Mining will have 25% chance to perform a critical swing (15% base chance + 10% chance from levelling benefits for runite). {| class="wikitable sortable" style="text-align:center;" |+ Level requirements for rock-specific critical swing chance increase |- ! rowspan="2" | Rock ! ... | [[Gorgonite rock]] |- | [[Promethium rock]] |} ====Critical swing bonus==== The critical swing bonus is the amount of extra damage gained for that swing. Although not every swing grants an ore, every swing grants experience based on the damage rolled for that swing. The damage made on that swing is multiplied by the experience multiplier of that rock and a global 0.4 to determine the base experience drop. Some Mining actions don't use this mechanic, but yield fixed number of experience like many other skills do. The [[world map]] now shows what rocks are available at each mining site. ** Mining rocks no longer deplete. ** Every swing now gives XP, but ore is only earned after filling up the progress bar with multiple swings. ** [[Rockertunities]] will spawn occasionally which, when clicked, result in a burst of additional XP and ore. ... ** [[Luck enhancers]] ([[ring of Wealth]], etc) now increase the chance for geodes to upgrade to [[metamorphic geodes]]. ** [[Quarrymaster aura]] now increases the chance to critically swing when mining. ... ** The [[mining accumulator]] now gains charge whenever the player gets a critical swing when mining. ** When mining, [[crystallise]] now only works on core mining rocks.
